hook: In nineteen nineteen, a giant wave of molasses swept through Boston.

blocks.narration: In nineteen nineteen, a giant wave of molasses swept through Boston. It sounds like a joke, but it was deadly.
blocks.visual: Cinematic storybook illustration of a 1919 Boston street, a huge dark tank looming over brick buildings, muted period palette

blocks.narration: It was January fifteenth, an unusually warm winter day in the North End, a busy neighborhood near the harbor.
blocks.visual: Illustrated crowds, horse carts and an elevated train track on a bright winter afternoon

blocks.narration: A huge storage tank held more than two million gallons of molasses, used to make industrial alcohol. It had leaked for years.
blocks.visual: Close illustration of rivets on a towering tank with dark streaks running down its sides

blocks.narration: Just after noon, witnesses heard a rumble like machine gun fire as the rivets popped. Then the tank burst open.
blocks.visual: Dramatic illustration of rivets flying as a dark wall erupts from the tank

blocks.narration: A wave of molasses, estimated up to twenty-five feet high, rushed through the streets at around thirty-five miles per hour.
blocks.visual: A towering dark brown wave crashes past buildings and toppled carts, archival paper texture

blocks.narration: It crushed buildings, bent the elevated railway, and trapped people and horses. Twenty-one people died and about one hundred fifty were injured.
blocks.visual: Somber illustration of rescuers wading through thick dark syrup among wreckage

blocks.narration: Courts later found the company responsible, and the case helped push stricter rules for engineering and building inspections in the years that followed.
blocks.visual: An illustrated courtroom with stacks of documents and a stern judge

blocks.narration: Locals claimed the area smelled sweet on hot days for decades. Follow for more history they skipped in school.
blocks.visual: Quiet modern waterfront park at sunset where the tank once stood, gentle pull back

captions.hook_line: In 1919, a wave of molasses swept through Boston. It was deadly 🌊
captions.body: On January 15, 1919, a storage tank in Boston's North End burst and released over two million gallons of molasses. A wave estimated up to 25 feet high killed 21 people and injured about 150. The company was later found liable.
